9. Evaluation Process 
The performance of a student in each semester shall be evaluated subject wise with a 
maximum of 100 marks for theory and 100 marks for practical subject. Summer 
Internships shall be evaluated for 50 marks, Full Internship &Project work in final 
semester shall be evaluated for 200 marks, mandatory courses with no credits shall be 
evaluated for 30 mid semester marks. 
 
A student has to secure not less than 35% of marks in the end examination and a 
minimum of 40% of marks in the sum total of the mid semester and end examination 
marks taken together for the theory, practical, design, drawing subject or project etc. In 
case of a mandatory course, he/she should secure 40% of the total marks.

11. Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs): 
 
A Student has to pursue and complete one course compulsorily through MOOCs 
approved by the University. A student can pursue courses other than core through 
MOOCs and it is mandatory to complete one course successfully through MOOCs for 
awarding the degree. A student is not permitted to register and pursue core courses 
through MOOCs. 
 
A student shall register for the course (Minimum of either 8 weeks or 12 weeks) offered 
through MOOCs with the approval of Head of the Department. The Head of the 
Department shall appoint one mentor to monitor the student’s progression. The student 
needs to earn a certificate by passing the exam. The student shall be awarded the credits 
assigned in the curriculum only by submission of the certificate. Examination fee, if 
any, will be borne by the student. 
 
 
Students who have qualified in the proctored examinations conducted through MOOCs 
platform can apply for credit transfer as specified and are exempted from appearing 
internal as well as external examination (for the specified equivalent credit course only) 
conducted by the university. 
 
 
Necessary amendments in rules and regulations regarding adoption of MOOC courses 
would be proposed from time to time. 
 
 
 
12.  Credit Transfer Policy 
 
Adoption of MOOCs is mandatory, to enable Blended model of teaching-learning as 
also envisaged in the NEP 2020. As per University Grants Commission (Credit 
Framework for Online Learning Courses through SWAYAM) Regulation, 2016, the 
University shall allow up to a maximum of 20% of the total courses being offered in a 
particular programme i.e., maximum of 32 credits through MOOCs platform. 
i) The University shall offer credit mobility for MOOCs and give the  equivalent 
credit weightage to the students for the credits earned through online learning 
courses.  
ii) Student registration for the MOOCs shall be only through the respective 
department of the institution, it is mandatory for the student to share necessary 
information with the department.  
iii) Credit transfer policy will be applicable to the Professional & Open Elective 
courses only.  
iv) The concerned department shall identify the courses permitted for credit 
transfer.  
v) The University/institution shall notify at the beginning of semester the list of the 
online learning courses eligible for credit transfer. 
vi) The institution shall designate a faculty member as a Mentor for each course to 
guide the students from registration till completion of the credit course. 
vii) The university shall ensure no overlap of MOOC exams with that of the 
university examination schedule. In case of delay in results, the university will 
re-issue the marks sheet for such students.

14. Mandatory Internships 
 
Summer Internships : Two summer internships either onsite or virtual each with a 
minimum of 08 weeks duration, done at the end of second and third years, respectively 
are mandatory. It shall be completed in collaboration with local industries, Govt. 
Organizations, construction agencies, Power projects, software MNCs or any industries 
in the areas of concerned specialization of the Undergraduate program. One of the two 
summer internships at the end of second year (Community Service Project) shall be 
society oriented and shall be completed in collaboration with government 
organizations/NGOs & others. The other internship at the end of third year is Industry 
Internship and shall be completed in collaboration with Industries. The student shall 
register for the internship as per course structure after commencement of academic year. 
The guidelines issued by the APSCHE / University shall be followed for carrying out 
and evaluation of Community Service Project and Industry Internship. 
 
Evaluation of the summer internships shall be through the departmental committee. A 
student will be required to submit a summer internship report to the concerned 
department and appear for an oral presentation before the departmental committee 
comprising of Head of the Department, supervisor of the internship and a senior faculty 
member of the department. A certificate of successful completion from industry shall

Computation of Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) and Cumulative Grade Point 
Average (CGPA): 
The Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) is the ratio of sum of the product of the 
number of credits with the grade points scored by a student in all the courses taken by 
a student and the sum of the number of credits of all the courses undergone by a student, 
i.e., 
SGPA = Σ (Ci × Gi)/Σ Ci 
where, Ci is the number of credits of the ith subject and Gi is the grade point 
scored by the student in the ith course. 
The Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) will be computed in the same manner 
considering all the courses undergone by a student over all the semesters of a program, 
i.e., 
CGPA = Σ (Ci × Si)/ Σ Ci 
where “Si” is the SGPA of the ith semester and Ci is the total number of credits 
up to that semester. 
Both SGPA and CGPA shall be rounded off to 2 decimal points and reported in the 
transcripts. 
While computing the SGPA the subjects in which the student is awarded Zero 
grade points will also be included. 
 
Grade Point: It is a numerical weight allotted to each letter grade on a 10-point scale. 
Letter Grade: It is an index of the performance of students in a said course. Grades are 
denoted by the letters S, A, B, C, D and F.

Course Objectives:

Course Outcomes: At the end of this course students will demonstrate the ability to

using Laplace transform.

Student Administrative Procedures 
 
1. How to Apply for a New ID Card in Case of Loss 
If your college ID card has been lost, follow the procedure below to apply for a replacement ID card: 
1. Write a formal request letter addressed to the Head of the Department (HOD), requesting a 
new ID card due to the loss of your existing card.  
2. Get the HOD's signature on the request letter.  
3. Get the Principal's signature on the duly signed request letter.  
4. Submit the signed letter to the Administration Office.  
5. Pay the prescribed fee for the replacement ID card at the Administration Office.  
6. The new ID card will generally be prepared within 2–3 working days.  
7. After the stipulated time, contact the concerned staff member at the Administration Office 
and collect your new ID card.  
Note: Keep the payment receipt or acknowledgement safely until you receive your new ID card. 
 
2. How to Apply for a New Regular ID Card After Vacating the College Hostel 
Students who are college hostel residents and wish to obtain a new regular ID card after vacating the 
hostel must complete the hostel vacation formalities before applying for the ID card. 
Follow these steps: 
1. Obtain the Hostel Vacation Letter/Form from the Hostel Warden as proof that you have 
vacated the college hostel.  
2. Get the Hostel Vacation Letter/Form signed by the Chief Warden.  
3. Write a formal request letter addressed to the HOD, requesting a new regular ID card.  
4. Get the HOD's signature on the request letter.  
5. Get the Principal's signature on the request letter.  
6. Submit the following documents to the Administration Office:  
o 
Duly signed request letter  
o 
Hostel Vacation Letter/Form signed by the Chief Warden  
7. Pay the prescribed fee for the new ID card.  
8. The new ID card will generally be prepared within 2–3 working days.  
9. After 2–3 working days, contact the concerned staff member at the Administration Office 
and collect your new regular ID card.

Important: The Hostel Vacation Letter/Form serves as proof that you have officially vacated the 
college hostel. 
 
3. How to Apply for a Bonafide Certificate 
To obtain a Bonafide Certificate, follow the procedure below: 
1. Write a formal request letter addressed to the HOD, requesting the issuance of a Bonafide 
Certificate.  
2. Consult the Administration Office and obtain the Fee Due Slip.  
3. If there are any applicable dues, mention the due amount/details on the request letter as 
instructed by the Administration Office.  
4. Get the HOD's signature on the request letter.  
5. Get the Principal's signature on the request letter.  
6. Consult your concerned department and submit the duly signed request letter to the 
Department DEO.  
7. The Department DEO will process the request and issue the Bonafide Certificate.  
8. Ensure that the certificate is printed on the official college letterhead.  
9. Carefully check all the details mentioned on the certificate, including:  
o 
Name  
o 
Roll/Registration Number  
o 
Course and Department  
o 
Academic year  
o 
Other relevant details  
10. After verifying the details, paste your passport-size photograph in the designated place on 
the certificate.  
11. Get the Bonafide Certificate signed by the principal.  
12. Once the Principal's signature is obtained, the Bonafide Certificate is ready for use.  
Important: Always verify your personal and academic details carefully before obtaining the final 
signature. Any errors should be corrected before the certificate is finalized.

4. How to Apply for a College Transfer Certificate (TC)? 
Students who are leaving the college or completing their course may need a Transfer Certificate. 
Procedure: 
1. Obtain the required TC application form from the Administration Office.  
2. Fill in all the required details correctly.  
3. Complete any required No-Due/Clearance formalities.  
4. Obtain the required signatures/approvals from the concerned departments.  
5. Submit the completed application to the Administration Office.  
6. Pay the prescribed fee, if applicable.  
7. Collect the Transfer Certificate after it has been prepared.  
 
5. How to Apply for a Conduct/Character Certificate? 
Procedure: 
1. Write a formal request letter or obtain the prescribed application form.  
2. Get the required recommendation/signature from the HOD.  
3. Complete any required No-Due formalities.  
4. Submit the application to the concerned office.  
5. The certificate will be prepared by the college.  
6. Collect the certificate after obtaining the required Principal's signature.  
 
6. How to Apply for a Study Certificate? 
Procedure: 
1. Write a formal request letter addressed to the HOD.  
2. Clearly mention the purpose for which the Study Certificate is required.  
3. Obtain the HOD's signature.  
4. Obtain the Principal's signature if required.  
5. Submit the request to the concerned department/Administration Office.  
6. Collect the Study Certificate after it has been prepared.  
 
7. How to Apply for a No-Due Certificate?

A No-Due Certificate confirms that the student has no outstanding dues or pending items with the 
college. 
Procedure: 
1. Obtain the No-Due/Clearance form from the concerned office.  
2. Obtain clearance from the required departments, such as:  
o 
Library  
o 
Hostel  
o 
Department  
o 
Accounts  
o 
Laboratory  
o 
Administration  
3. Ensure that all required signatures/stamps are obtained.  
4. Submit the completed form to the Administration/Accounts Office.  
5. Collect the No-Due Certificate after verification.  
 
8. How to Obtain a Fee Due/Payment Statement? 
Procedure: 
1. Visit the Accounts/Administration Office.  
2. Request the Fee Due/Payment Statement.  
3. Provide your student ID/Roll Number if required.  
4. The office will verify your account.  
5. Collect the statement or fee details after verification.  
 
9. How to Apply for a Fee Receipt? 
Procedure: 
1. Visit the Accounts Office.  
2. Provide your student details or payment reference.  
3. Request the fee receipt.  
4. Verify the amount, academic year, semester, and student details.  
5. Collect the receipt.

10. How to Correct a Mistake in College Records? 
If there is an error in your name, date of birth, parent's name, address, course, or other academic 
details: 
1. Identify the incorrect information.  
2. Prepare a formal request letter explaining the correction required.  
3. Attach the appropriate supporting document/proof.  
4. Submit the request to the concerned department/Administration Office.  
5. Obtain the required approvals/signatures.  
6. The college will verify the documents and update the records.  
Examples of supporting documents: Aadhaar card, SSC certificate, passport, or other officially 
accepted documents, depending on the correction. 
 
11. How to Apply for a Change of Address or Contact Details? 
Procedure: 
1. Obtain the prescribed form or write a formal request letter.  
2. Mention the old and new details clearly.  
3. Attach supporting proof if required.  
4. Submit the request to the Administration Office.  
5. Verify that the updated information has been entered correctly.  
 
12. How to Apply for a Bonafide Certificate for a Bank/Education Loan? 
Follow the regular Bonafide Certificate procedure, but clearly mention the purpose, such as: 
• 
Education loan  
• 
Bank account  
• 
Scholarship  
• 
Passport  
• 
Internship  
• 
Visa  
• 
Government application  
Make sure the purpose is correctly mentioned because the certificate may need to contain specific 
information.

13. How to Apply for a Student Verification Letter? 
Procedure: 
1. Write a formal request stating the purpose of the verification letter.  
2. Obtain the required HOD/department approval.  
3. Submit the request to the concerned department or Administration Office.  
4. Provide any supporting documents if required.  
5. Collect the verification letter after it is issued.  
 
14. How to Apply for a Duplicate Certificate? 
If an original college-issued certificate has been lost or damaged: 
1. Report the loss to the concerned authority if required.  
2. Write a formal request for a duplicate certificate.  
3. Provide details of the original certificate.  
4. Submit supporting documents or an affidavit/loss report if required.  
5. Complete the required approvals.  
6. Pay the prescribed fee, if applicable.  
7. Collect the duplicate certificate after processing.  
 
15. How to Apply for a Migration Certificate? 
Procedure: 
1. Obtain the Migration Certificate application form.  
2. Fill in the required details.  
3. Complete the required No-Due/Clearance formalities.  
4. Submit the application and supporting documents.  
5. Pay the prescribed fee, if applicable.  
6. Collect the Migration Certificate after it is issued.  
 
16. How to Apply for a Scholarship Certificate/Document? 
Procedure: 
1. Check the scholarship requirements.  
2. Identify the documents required from the college.

3. Submit a request to the concerned department/Administration Office.  
4. Provide your student and scholarship details.  
5. Obtain the required certificate/document.  
6. Verify all details before submitting it to the scholarship authority.  
 
17. How to Apply for a Hostel Bonafide/Hostel Residence Certificate? 
Procedure: 
1. Contact the Hostel Office/Warden.  
2. Submit a request for the Hostel Residence Certificate.  
3. Provide your hostel and student details.  
4. Obtain the required Warden/Chief Warden verification.  
5. Collect the certificate after it is issued.  
 
18. How to Apply for Hostel Leave? 
Procedure: 
1. Submit the prescribed hostel leave application.  
2. Mention the reason, destination, dates, and expected return date.  
3. Obtain the required approval from the Hostel Warden.  
4. If required, obtain parent/guardian approval.  
5. Submit the approved leave form to the Hostel Office before leaving.  
 
19. How to Apply for Hostel Vacating Formalities? 
Procedure: 
1. Inform the Hostel Warden about your intention to vacate.  
2. Complete the prescribed hostel vacation form.  
3. Return hostel keys and any college/hostel property issued to you.  
4. Clear pending hostel dues.  
5. Obtain the required clearance/signature from the Warden.  
6. Obtain the Chief Warden's signature.  
7. Collect the Hostel Vacation/Leaving document.  
8. Complete the college No-Due formalities if required.

20. How to Apply for a Semester/College Leave? 
Procedure: 
1. Write a formal leave request mentioning the reason and duration.  
2. Submit it to the HOD/class coordinator as applicable.  
3. Attach supporting documents if required.  
4. Obtain the necessary approval.  
5. Submit the approved leave request to the concerned office.  
 
21. What Should I Do If I Lose My College Documents? 
If you lose an important college document: 
1. Immediately inform the concerned department/Administration Office.  
2. Identify exactly which document has been lost.  
3. Submit a formal written request.  
4. Provide supporting details/documents.  
5. Complete any required loss declaration or police complaint formalities.  
6. Pay the prescribed duplicate-document fee, if applicable.  
7. Collect the replacement document after verification.  
 
22. How to Apply for a Certificate for Internship or Industrial Training? 
Procedure: 
1. Obtain the internship/industrial training requirement or request from the organization.  
2. Submit a request letter to the HOD.  
3. Mention the organization, training period, and purpose.  
4. Obtain the required approval.  
5. Submit the request to the concerned department/Administration Office.  
6. Collect the required permission/certificate.  
 
23. How to Get an Attendance Certificate? 
Procedure: 
1. Contact your concerned department.

2. Submit a formal request if required.  
3. Provide your roll number, course, semester, and academic year.  
4. The department will verify your attendance records.  
5. Collect the Attendance Certificate after it is issued.  
 
24. How to Apply for a Late Fee Payment/Extension? 
If you are unable to pay your college fee within the prescribed deadline: 
1. Contact the Accounts Office immediately.  
2. Submit a formal request explaining the reason for the delay.  
3. Attach supporting documents if required.  
4. Obtain the required approval.  
5. Pay the applicable fee and late fee, if permitted.  
6. Collect the payment receipt.
